messages:
pagerduty-bot: P1 ALERT — GPU capacity exhausted in prod-us-west-2. Autoscaler failed to add GPU nodes; queue length on inference service 'inference-gpu' increasing rapidly. Paging @oncall. Incident runbook: https://redwood/runbooks/gpu-capacity

nina: I’m on it. seeing spike in queued requests to /v1/generate across multiple routes. latency + error 503 on dedicated customers. grabbing logs now.

sam: @nina any signs of ASG activity? can we see scale up attempts?

nina: ops-bot posted CA events — autoscaler trying to create nodes but instances never register. no successful scaleup in last 12m.

ops-bot: cluster-autoscaler event snippet:
```
I0523 14:03:10.123456 1 autoprovision.go:324] Scale-up: adding 1 nodes to group gpustatic-prod-pt-1
E0523 14:04:02.987654 1 cloud_provider.go:212] Failed to create node from launch template: InvalidInstanceMetadataOptions: Instance Metadata Service v2 required
caused by: launch template requires IMDSv2, request used IMDSv1
E0523 14:04:03.000000 1 node_registration.go:67] node never registered: timeout waiting for kubelet
```

raj: huh — our launch template recently hardened IMDS to v2 only to mitigate token theft. CA is using the AWS SDK default which should support IMDSv2. maybe the bootstrap user-data is still calling IMDSv1. checking AMI userdata logs via console.

sam: also seeing kubelet failures on the few nodes that did boot: kubelet failing to register due to mismatched kubelet certs — looks like cloud-init sometimes skips kubeadm join when userdata fails at IMDS call.

nina: impact: three large Dedicated customers seeing generation latency > 10s and some timed-out requests. non-blocking for lower-priority CPU routes but P1 because realtime customers impacted.

eng-infra: confirmed — we pushed launch template change last week enabling metadata options: { "HttpTokens": "required" }. Boot scripts attempt to fetch instance metadata with `curl http://169.254.169.254/latest/meta-data/` without IMDSv2 token, so it fails and userdata aborts before kubeadm join.

maria: plan: short-term mitigate by creating a temporary launch template variant that allows IMDSv1 (HttpTokens: optional) and a manual nodepool to get GPUs back online. medium-term: patch userdata to use IMDSv2 token flow and update CA container to enforce IMDSv2 when provisioning.

sam: +1 to manual nodepool. can infra spin up a nodegroup from existing LT vX that uses optional tokens? if yes, we can attach and drain spot pools to reduce queue.

eng-infra: spinning up manual nodegroup now with LT fallback (HttpTokens=optional). command:
```
aws autoscaling create-auto-scaling-group --auto-scaling-group-name prod-temp-gpu-334 --launch-template LaunchTemplateId=lt-0abcd,Version=1 --min-size 1 --max-size 10 --desired-capacity 2 --tags Key=Name,Value=prod-temp-gpu
```

ops-bot: Manual nodegroup creation started. Expect nodes to be healthy in ~4-6 minutes. Routing decisions: redis queue consumer will pick up backpressure once nodes register.

nina: while that comes up, throttle non-critical batch jobs and reduce max tokens for public hosted routes to limit additional pressure. I've toggled batch-worker scale to minimum.

raj: noticed CA logs also showing `access denied to iam:PassRole` on some scale attempts — cross-checking. if autoscaler role lacks PassRole for new launch template, it would fail. but current failure seems primarily IMDS boot-strictness + userdata.

sam: good catch — eng-infra, please confirm autoscaler IAM has PassRole on new launch template variants before we make them default.

eng-infra: confirmed autoscaler role has PassRole for role arn:aws:iam::123456:role/RedwoodNodeRole but not for the new profile we used last month. we will add policy in parallel.

maria: update: manual nodegroup reached Ready, kubelet registered, nodes labeled `redwood/gpu=true`. I’m uncordoning a few pods to let traffic drain from queues.

nina: seeing queue length stabilize and error rate drop. latency for affected customers improving. tagging incident as mitigated for now.

sam: follow-ups: (1) update userdata to IMDSv2 token flow (2) ensure autoscaler handles IMDSv2 kick (3) add test where LT requires IMDSv2 in our staging autoscaler tests (4) attach PassRole policy to autoscaler role for all LT variants (5) run a rolling launchtemplate bump with canary.

raj: assigning follow-ups to eng-infra and eng-oncall. I’ll open Jira PBI and link runbook.

maria: handing to next oncall @eve for overnight monitoring. please monitor queue metric `inference.queue.size` and ASG events.

eve: ack. I’ll watch dashboards and escalate if queue > 100 or >5 failed scale attempts.

pagerduty-bot: Incident status: mitigated — manual nodepool added and ingress throttles applied. Postmortem required within 48h.

nina: thanks team — good coordination. adding notes to postmortem: root cause = userdata IMDSv1 calls + LT HttpTokens=required + CA/userdata mismatch + missing PassRole on one profile.
